- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 1.5x recent high or adjust downward 1–3% after spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is trending up, model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates in early horizon (1–3 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply slight upward bias (0.5–1.5%) for short-term forecasts.
- When sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “negative” values, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to catch mean reversion or rebound.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome over 3–5 days, apply “mean reversion” correction: add 0.5–1.5% per day to forecast until convergence with true trend.
- For long-term (15+ day) forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often overfits recent noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ true values or apply 1–2% downward bias.
